author: WP09
summary: Older WebGPU campaign narrative: native 2D baseline, pixel-assertion lessons, PbrEffect, render targets, cube targets, mip generation, the BC gap, three former limitations and an open-items list. Largely stale at 009d40f5: MRT, stencil baking, wireframe, custom SpriteBatch and WGSL effects, cube mips and MSAA, BC upload, the browser route and a non-sRGB surface policy all exist. Tutorial 132 already covered build, capabilities and formats; current renderer semantics and the historical lessons were written into a WebGPU deep dive.

concepts.section: Legacy WebGPU Chapter Material
concepts.text: WEBGPU targets a pinned wgpu-native v29.0.1.1 natively and is selected with -DCNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER=WEBGPU like every other identity.

concepts.section: Legacy WebGPU Chapter Material
concepts.text: WEBGPU was the youngest renderer when written up, implemented after the project owner lifted an earlier prohibition, with a plan of fourteen phases and over 130 numbered tasks.
concepts.note: Project chronology and plan size; not current technical documentation.

concepts.section: What ``experimental'' concretely means here
concepts.text: At the time of writing WEBGPU was excluded from the cross-renderer feature matrix because its surface was not yet broad enough for a side-by-side comparison.
concepts.note: Superseded status: at 009d40f5 WEBGPU registers the 32-fixture parity corpus and reports MRT, queries, wireframe and compute; recorded as a separate PRESERVED concept.

concepts.section: What ``experimental'' concretely means here
concepts.text: At the snapshot WEBGPU is declared Experimental by CNA and takes part in the shared cross-renderer parity corpus as WebGPU_Parity_ tests, whose oracle is each fixture's own assertions.

concepts.section: The native 2D baseline
concepts.text: The native 2D baseline covers device and surface setup, clear and present, Texture2D, buffer uploads and a WGSL SpriteBatch, checked by a 120-frame smoke run and a deterministic SpriteBatch validation scene (cropping, tint and alpha, rotation, flips, filtering, address modes).

concepts.section: The native 2D baseline
concepts.text: An independently developed XNA-style game port (Speedy Blupi, mobile-eggbert) reached its main menu and played an animated cutscene on WEBGPU without validation errors.
concepts.note: Evidence for a sibling repository at its own revision, not for 009d40f5 and not re-verifiable from the CNA tree; the site's truthfulness rules forbid presenting it as TARGET evidence.

concepts.section: A bug a manual screenshot review missed, and a pixel assertion caught
concepts.text: WebGPU's SpriteBatch pipeline blend factors did not match the shader's non-premultiplied output, so translucent sprites rendered opaque; fixed by matching Vulkan's blend-factor pairing.
concepts.note: Fixed; the SpriteBatch pipeline now bakes the full blend state (WebGPUSpriteBlendSnapshot); kept on the page as a historical lesson.

concepts.section: A bug a manual screenshot review missed, and a pixel assertion caught
concepts.text: Methodological lesson: a manual screenshot review can miss a measurable error (translucency) that a pixel-value assertion catches.
tokens: A review that looks instead of measuring

concepts.section: 3D depth testing and the gap it exposed
concepts.text: Before WebGPU's first 3D route, verified with a real near/far depth-ordering test, the renderer's depth-stencil apply entry point was unimplemented, so DepthStencilState silently did nothing on WEBGPU.
concepts.note: Fixed: depth and stencil state are baked per pipeline (WEBGPU-39, WEBGPU-83).

concepts.section: 3D depth testing and the gap it exposed
concepts.text: WEBGPU implements every stock effect including PbrEffect and the skinned SkinnedEffect and SkinnedPbrEffect variants (72-bone palette, SkinnedEffect::MaxBones), ported from EasyGL's shaders.

concepts.section: PbrEffect: a CNAEXT metallic-roughness material
concepts.text: PbrEffect is a CNAEXT glTF 2.0 metallic-roughness material with no XNA counterpart; it combines the IEffectMatrices, IEffectLights and IEffectFog plumbing with base-colour, normal, metallic-roughness, occlusion and emissive maps and multiplying factors.

concepts.section: PbrEffect: a CNAEXT metallic-roughness material
concepts.text: The metallic-roughness map follows glTF's own packing (green roughness, blue metallic), so conformant exports bind without repacking.
tokens: green is roughness, blue is metallic

concepts.section: PbrEffect: a CNAEXT metallic-roughness material
concepts.text: A glTF character rig with a metallic-roughness material reaches GPU skinning through SkinnedPbrEffect rather than SkinnedEffect.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: The source unit said WebGPU RenderTarget2D combines depth and stencil into one format regardless of the request; at the snapshot MapDepthFormatEXT (WEBGPU-39) maps each target's DepthFormat exactly and None means no depth attachment.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: A WebGPU MSAA test that appeared to fail was a defect in the test itself (a missing RasterizerState::CullNone), not in the implementation.
tokens: A failing test can be the defect
concepts.note: Kept as a labelled historical lesson; not re-verified.

target.evidence: CNA plan history; not re-derivable from the test file at 009d40f5

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: WebGPU instancing uses a real per-instance vertex stream needing no bind-group change, and several vertex streams of one input rate each get their own native vertex-buffer layout (WEBGPU-172).

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: WebGPU's SpriteBatch queue path once computed clip-space positions from the back buffer's logical size even while a differently sized target was bound; REMED-GFX-019 now selects the bound 2D target, cube face or back-buffer logical viewport before converting.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: wgpu-native v29 has no filtered blit, so WebGPU generates mip levels with a full-screen-triangle render pass per level sampling the previous level linearly.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: WebGPU regenerates a plain Texture2D or TextureCube chain after every level-0 write (WEBGPU-52), a documented divergence from XNA, FNA and the other renderers that can overwrite upper levels a game authored earlier.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: The source unit said SDL_GPU is the narrow exception that auto-generates mips for plain cubes after a complete level-0 face upload; at the snapshot SDL_GPU's plain TextureCube is a SAMPLER-only authored-level resource that never calls SDL's generator.
concepts.note: Only rendered targets regenerate chains on SDL_GPU; plain textures are authored, as in XNA and FNA.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: Render-target mip generation on WebGPU is a separate contract: RenderTarget2D regenerates on unbind (WEBGPU-164) and RenderTargetCube per face after its pass (WEBGPU-114).

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: The source unit said WebGPU's default surface prefers BGRA8-sRGB then RGBA8-sRGB, the opposite policy from Vulkan.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 REMED-GFX-131 prefers the UNORM formats and reinterprets an sRGB-only surface through view formats; the page documents both the current policy and the history.

concepts.section: Render targets, environment mapping, instancing, and mip generation
concepts.text: WebGPU's back-buffer depth texture is always Depth24PlusStencil8, recreated for each non-minimised surface with the colour sample count, even for DepthFormat::None; requested presentation formats do not participate; a fullscreen transition is performed by the platform window and the next frame reconfigures the surface.

concepts.section: The corrected render-target-size trap
concepts.text: Worked example of the former render-target-size trap: a SpriteBatch draw intended to fill a small off-screen target was scaled and placed as though the target were the window, with no error.

concepts.section: The corrected render-target-size trap
concepts.text: WebGPU_SpriteBatch_RenderTarget pairs a 96x72 back buffer with 48x32 and 64x40 targets, covers target/back buffer isolation, a transform, orientation and a 48x48 cube face, and requires probe pixels inside the old wrong rectangle to stay black.

concepts.section: RenderTargetCube and its former silent cast failure
concepts.text: WebGPU RenderTargetCube (WEBGPU-114): one six-layer texture, a 2D view per face for rendering and one cube view for sampling, and one depth-stencil attachment shared by all faces with a matching sample count.

concepts.section: RenderTargetCube and its former silent cast failure
concepts.text: EnvironmentMapEffect's environment map was hard-coded to the concrete TextureCube renderer type, so binding a RenderTargetCube silently sampled the 1x1 white cube; the IWebGPUCubeSamplable interface and a single dynamic_cast fixed it, and deferred draws now store its SampledCube() keep-alive value (REMED-GFX-167).

concepts.section: RenderTargetCube and its former silent cast failure
concepts.text: webgpu_rendertargetcube_test.cpp Check C samples a blue-cleared cube through EnvironmentMapEffect and Check D proves back-buffer and cube-face clears do not leak into each other.

concepts.section: RenderTargetCube and its former silent cast failure
concepts.text: The source unit's two cube scope cuts (mipMap=true throws; MSAA ignored and reported as 0) no longer hold: cube targets allocate and regenerate a full chain per face and honour a per-cube sample count (WEBGPU-165); the test's header comment is stale.
concepts.note: Current behaviour is written on the page; the stale test header comment is noted.

concepts.section: Why block-compressed texture upload remains open
concepts.text: Block-compressed upload was blocked above the renderer: content loading decompressed DXT to RGBA8 and ImageData had no surface-format field, although the development adapter supported TextureCompressionBC.
concepts.note: Historical diagnosis kept as history on the page; the gap is closed at 009d40f5.

concepts.section: Why block-compressed texture upload remains open
concepts.text: A WebGPU-only shortcut (raw BC bytes in the RGBA8-typed ImageData field) was rejected because no real game's loading path could produce it and it would misrepresent the data contract; the fix had to be a cross-renderer design change.

concepts.section: Why block-compressed texture upload remains open
concepts.text: At the snapshot WebGPU uploads DXT and BC7 content natively when the device enabled the BC feature (WEBGPU-144, cubes WEBGPU-206), the content loaders keep such content compressed through LoadsCompressedContentNativelyEXT and IsCompressedTransferFormatEXT, and ImageData carries surfaceFormat and mipLevels.

concepts.section: Why block-compressed texture upload remains open
concepts.text: A diagnostic run on the development GPU found wgpuAdapterHasFeature(TextureCompressionBC) true and a device with that feature creatable.
concepts.note: Host-specific measurement on one machine at an older revision; not TARGET evidence and not re-runnable here.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: WebGPUTextureRenderer::GetData (WEBGPU-51) copies a mip level into a MapRead buffer with 256-byte row alignment, waits for the asynchronous map and extracts the rectangle; its test drives IGraphicsRenderer directly because the public Texture2D serves a CPU shadow.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: WebGPU cull mode is part of the 3D pipeline key; with a counter-clockwise pipeline front face and framebuffer-space facing, CullClockwiseFace maps to WGPUCullMode_Back and CullCounterClockwiseFace to WGPUCullMode_Front (REMED-GFX-160); the earlier mapping was inverted by a probe with mis-derived winding.
concepts.note: The source unit presented the differential cull test as proving the mapping; TARGET records that the earlier 'verified' mapping was wrong.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: WebGPU viewport and scissor are per-command dynamic state captured at the draw call (REMED-GFX-116/146), applied through the two native setters with redundant calls skipped; cardinality tests prove no pipeline variant, pass split or per-draw setter was needed.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: WebGPU clamps the viewport to the target at application time because wgpu-native rejects an oversized viewport and GraphicsDevice.Viewport can be stale across a live resize; a disabled scissor is the whole target while an enabled zero-area scissor stays zero-area and clips everything.
concepts.note: The source unit said a disabled or zero scissor expands to the full target; at TARGET only a disabled scissor does.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: The source unit said WEBGPU refuses FillMode.WireFrame for polygon draws because WebGPU has no polygon mode.
concepts.note: Wireframe is emulated by expanding triangle edges into a line-list index buffer on every 3D route.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: The source unit said WEBGPU stores the stencil configuration but has not baked stencil operations into its pipelines.
concepts.note: Stencil operations are baked per pipeline with a dynamic per-draw reference.

concepts.section: Three former limitations that are no longer true
concepts.text: Lesson: a plausible state mapping without an equivalent differential pixel test can make an invisible error look implemented, and even a differential test needs an oracle derived from the reference contract.
tokens: An oracle derived from the wrong contract

concepts.section: Clear ordering and usage are consistent across target types
concepts.text: WebGPU replays all eleven deferred draw families and every public Clear in one ordered stream (REMED-GFX-159); leading clears fold into the next segment's load actions and a clear after a draw closes the segment.

concepts.section: Clear ordering and usage are consistent across target types
concepts.text: WebGPU usage: the shared FNA predicate decides discard; the first native segment selects clear or load for colour, depth and stencil together, later segments load unless an explicit clear selects an aspect; a cube face owns its colour view and all faces share depth.

concepts.section: Clear ordering and usage are consistent across target types
concepts.text: The back buffer has no RenderTargetUsage in WebGPU's off-screen policy (its first segment is never treated as discarded); the source unit's statement that plural binding still rejects MRT is stale because MRT is implemented.

concepts.section: What remains open
concepts.text: The source unit listed as open on WEBGPU: multiple render targets, stencil-operation mapping, WireFrame, custom SpriteBatch effects and custom WGSL effects.
concepts.note: All five are implemented at 009d40f5; the page lists them as closed gaps.

concepts.section: What remains open
concepts.text: WebGPU BlendState is complete for keyed SpriteBatch and 3D pipelines: all factors and operations, dynamic BlendFactor, MultiSampleMask and per-slot ColorWriteChannels (WEBGPU-143) now that MRT exists.
concepts.note: The source unit said slots 1-3 were inapplicable until MRT existed.

concepts.section: What remains open
concepts.text: WebGPU occlusion queries are real (WEBGPU-84): the query records a begin and end pair around its draws and resolves an exact sample count.
concepts.note: Older CNA audit material recorded WEBGPU claiming OcclusionQuery while returning null; not so at TARGET.

concepts.section: What remains open
concepts.text: The source unit said browser WebGPU is entirely out of scope and the renderer is native wgpu-native only.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 a browser route through the Emscripten emdawnwebgpu port exists; Tutorial 132 documents it.

concepts.section: What remains open
concepts.text: The source unit said no renderer anywhere does real block-compressed texture upload.
concepts.note: WEBGPU and VULKAN (with textureCompressionBC) upload BC natively at 009d40f5.

concepts.section: Verification methodology, and how it differs from D3D9's
concepts.text: WebGPU verification is a native CTest set that skips without a usable display or adapter, per-feature pixel assertions and scripted browser runs; it is not compared with real XNA output, which exists only for DIRECTX9.

issues.text: WebGPU regenerates plain Texture2D/TextureCube mips after every level-0 write, overwriting upper levels a game authored earlier; documented in source as a deliberate divergence from XNA/FNA.
WebGPU's back buffer always has a Depth24PlusStencil8 attachment but PresentationParameters keeps the requested DepthFormat (no applied-format override), unlike Vulkan's VULKAN-348 write-back.
webgpu_rendertargetcube_test.cpp's header comment still describes mipMap=true as throwing and cube MSAA as reporting 0, contradicting its own current checks.
WEBGPU is selected by no CI workflow; native evidence is Linux x86_64 only and browser evidence is scripted headless Chrome.
WebGPU SpriteBatch blend factors did not match the shader's non-premultiplied output, rendering translucent sprites opaque.
WebGPU's depth-stencil apply entry point was unimplemented, so DepthStencilState did nothing.
WebGPU SpriteBatch positions were computed from the back buffer's size while a differently sized render target was bound.
Binding a RenderTargetCube as EnvironmentMapEffect.EnvironmentMap on WebGPU silently sampled the 1x1 white cube.
WebGPU preferred an sRGB surface format, gamma-encoding SurfaceFormat::Color in the back buffer and render targets.
No renderer uploaded block-compressed textures natively (ImageData RGBA8 only; DXT decompressed on load).
WebGPU lacked MRT, stencil-operation baking, WireFrame, custom SpriteBatch effects and custom WGSL effects.
WebGPU RenderTargetCube refused mipMap=true and ignored MultiSampleCount (reported 0).
WebGPU was native wgpu-native only; browser WebGPU out of scope.
